Complete Tutorial

Everything you need to know — from reading basic radar to tracking hurricane hunters in real time.

Overview Tabs Layers Alerts Overlays SPC Tropical Models Tools Pro Tips
🗺️
OVERVIEW
Understanding the interface

GWCFC Radar is a live weather map built around a Leaflet map that fills your entire screen. Everything else — controls, legends, overlays — floats on top of the map so the data always takes center stage.

Interface Map
↖ Top-left
Mode tabs (Regular, Tropical)
↗ Top-right
Mode tabs (Severe, Ice)
← Left sidebar
Layer controls — toggle on/off individually
↙ Bottom-right
Precipitation legend + overlay pill bar
↙ Bottom-left
Animation scrubber & playback controls
↑ Top-center
GWCFC logo — click to open quick menu (Search, Settings, Tutorial, Profile)

The map uses a tile-based system — you can zoom, pan, and rotate freely. Pinch to zoom on mobile, use a three-finger twist gesture to rotate. A compass and ↺ Reset button appear when rotated; tap Reset to snap back to north-up.

💡
First time here? Start with the Regular tab active (it is by default). You'll see live NEXRAD radar and current weather alerts. From there, layer on what you need.
🗂️
THE FOUR TABS
Modes that change the sidebar & available layers

The four square buttons in the top corners switch you between major weather modes. Each mode loads a different set of layers in the sidebar. Your overlays (lightning, cams, etc.) stay active across modes.

Tab Icons — top-left and top-right corners
🌩
Regular
🌀
Tropical
⚠
Severe
❄️

🌩
REGULAR

The everyday tab. Access Radar (Reflectivity/Velocity), GOES Satellite (IR/Visible/Water Vapor), NWS Alerts, Wind barbs, Temp, Waves, and Pressure. Overlay pills add Lightning, Webcams, Radio, Forecast Dots, and Hurricane Hunters on top. Best for day-to-day monitoring.

🌀
TROPICAL

Hurricane season mode. Same base layers as Regular, plus a Models bubble that opens the tropical model viewer (GFS, ECMWF, HWRF, HAFS, and more). NHC forecast cones, invest areas, and SST load automatically with the tab. Built for storm tracking.

⚠
SEVERE

Same base layers as Regular, plus a Models bubble that opens the severe model panel (SREF, HREF, NAM, HRRR). SPC Day 1/2/3 outlooks are available as sub-menu options under the Alerts bubble.

❄️
ICE

Winter storm mode. Ice accumulation forecasts, winter watches/warnings, and model guidance for freezing rain and snowfall.

📡
LAYERS
The left sidebar — click any row to toggle

The left sidebar holds floating bubble buttons for each data layer. Tap a bubble to turn it on — it glows cyan when active. Most bubbles open a secondary sub-menu (e.g. tapping Radar lets you choose Reflectivity or Velocity; tapping Satellite lets you choose IR, Visible, or Water Vapor). Note that Radar and Satellite are mutually exclusive — turning one on disables the other.

Actual sidebar bubbles — active bubble glows cyan
📡 Radar LIVE
🛰 Satellite GOES
⚠ Alerts NWS
💨 Wind BARBS
🌡 Temp 2M
📡
RADAR

Tap to choose Reflectivity (precipitation intensity) or Velocity (wind motion toward/away from the radar). Composite mosaic from NOAA's WSR-88D network — updated every 2 minutes. Station labels like KTLX (Oklahoma City), KEWX (San Antonio), and KAMX (Miami) appear at close zoom levels.

🛰
SATELLITE

Tap to choose Infrared, Visible, or Water Vapor imagery, then pick a region (CONUS, Global, Atlantic, Alaska, Hawaii, Full Disk, or Mesoscale). Radar and Satellite are mutually exclusive — enabling one disables the other.

⚠
ALERTS

Opens a sub-menu for WX Alerts (NWS watches, warnings, and advisories drawn as county polygons on the map) and EAS Alerts (live Emergency Alert System broadcasts). Each alert polygon is clickable for the full NWS alert text.

💨
WIND

Opens a sub-menu for Regular wind barbs (sustained 10m wind speed and direction) and Gusts (peak gust barbs). Barbs load instantly using Open-Meteo — a first pass of ~50 barbs appears within ~250ms, then expands to hundreds covering both land and ocean. Arrow points in the wind direction; color scales from blue (calm) through green/yellow to red/purple (severe). Click any barb for speed in mph/kt, direction, and gust info.

🌡
TEMP

Plots 2-meter air temperature markers across the map. Useful for seeing warm/cold sectors, frontal boundaries, and temperature contrasts ahead of and behind storm systems.

🔵
PRESSURE

Overlays surface pressure data. Useful for identifying high and low pressure centers, fronts, and the pressure gradient that drives wind. Pair with Wind barbs to see the full picture.

📶
Reading reflectivity colors: Blues and greens are light precipitation (under ~20 mm/hr). Yellow and orange mean moderate to heavy rain. Red (50+ dBZ) indicates heavy rain or large hail. Purple/magenta indicates extreme returns — hail cores or very intense rainfall above 75 mm/hr. On Velocity, green shades move toward the radar, red/orange shades move away — a tight green/red couplet indicates rotation.
Precipitation color scale (mm/h)
LightModerateHeavyIntenseExtreme
🚨
WEATHER ALERTS
Warnings, watches & advisories from NWS

Alerts are overlaid directly on the map as semi-transparent polygons matching the exact county or zone boundaries issued by the National Weather Service. They update in near real-time.

Tornado Warning — most urgent, take shelter immediately
Severe Thunderstorm Warning — damaging wind/hail
Tornado Watch — conditions favorable, stay alert
Severe Thunderstorm Watch — broad area at risk
Flood Warning — flooding occurring or imminent
Mesoscale Discussion — SPC analysis, not yet a watch
⚠️
Warning vs. Watch: A Warning means a hazard is occurring or imminent — take action now. A Watch means conditions are favorable — stay aware and be ready to act.

Each alert polygon on the map is clickable — tap or click it to open a popup with the full NWS alert text, including the affected areas, timing, and hazard details.

Use the Alerts Panel (visible in the sidebar depending on your tab) to see a full list of active alerts sorted by severity. There is also a "past alerts" toggle to review recently expired warnings.

📻 EAS Alerts

The EAS (Emergency Alert System) panel shows active emergency broadcasts from radio stations in your area. These are the same alerts broadcast over the air during severe weather. Each entry shows the station, the alert type, and the broadcast text.

💡
Meso discussions: Toggle the Meso layer to see NWS Mesoscale Discussions — these are issued before a watch is needed and give you 30–90 minutes of lead time on developing severe weather.
🎛️
OVERLAY BAR
Quick-toggle extras — bottom-right corner

The small pill buttons above the precipitation legend toggle extra data overlays that complement any tab. They stay active across tab switches.

⚡
LIGHTNING

Plots live lightning strike locations as they occur. Each strike appears as a small bolt. Also toggle LTG 30 in the sidebar to show the last 30-minute history with fading intensity.

📷
WEBCAMS

Places camera icons at webcam locations. Click any camera icon to open a floating panel with a live feed. EarthCam provides YouTube-powered live streams from around the world (city skylines, beaches, landmarks). WSDOT provides Pacific Northwest DOT traffic cameras with live snapshots. The camera panel is draggable — grab the title bar to reposition it anywhere on screen.

📻
RADIO STATIONS
🌥️
FORECAST DOTS

Shows hourly point forecasts as small dot markers across the map. Click any dot to see temperature, wind, precipitation chance, and conditions for that location. On by default.

🛩️
HURRICANE HUNTERS

Tracks NOAA's WP-3D Orion and G-IV aircraft in real time via ADS-B Exchange (free, no key required). Aircraft positions update every 60 seconds. Active recon planes include N42RF "Kermit" and N43RF "Miss Piggy" (WP-3D Orions that penetrate storm eyewalls) and N49RF "Gonzo" (a G-IV that surveys the upper atmosphere around the storm). If no aircraft are airborne, a brief notice appears and clears automatically.

🛩️
Hurricane Hunters: Tap the 🛩️ pill to activate live tracking via ADS-B Exchange — no API key or account needed. NOAA's WP-3D Orions (N42RF "Kermit", N43RF "Miss Piggy") and G-IV jet (N49RF "Gonzo") appear as plane icons when airborne. Click any aircraft for its call sign, altitude, speed, and heading. During Hurricane Milton (Oct 2024), Kermit flew through the eyewall at 1,500 ft while the storm was Cat 5 — visible in real time on this layer. If no aircraft are airborne, a brief notice appears and clears automatically.
⚠️
SPC OUTLOOKS
Severe tab — Storm Prediction Center risk areas

Switch to the Severe tab (⚠) to access Storm Prediction Center outlooks. SPC issues categorical and probabilistic outlooks for Days 1, 2, and 3 — indicating where conditions favor severe thunderstorms.

General — general thunderstorms possible; no organized severe weather expected
Slight (SLGT) — scattered severe storms likely; well-organized activity possible
Enhanced (ENH) — numerous severe storms expected
Moderate (MDT) — significant severe weather outbreak likely
High (HIGH) — particularly dangerous situation (PDS) — rare

Toggle SPC Day 1, Day 2, and Day 3 independently. Day 1 is the current day's outlook (updated several times daily); Day 2 covers tomorrow; Day 3 covers the day after.

⚠️
Moderate or High Risk? These are rare events — issued only when SPC is highly confident in a widespread severe weather outbreak. A High risk day means a particularly dangerous situation (PDS) is expected. Notable historic High Risk days include April 27, 2011 (the 2011 Super Outbreak — 211 tornadoes in one day, including the EF5 that struck Tuscaloosa and Birmingham, AL) and May 20, 2013 (EF5 Moore, OK tornado, 1.3-mile-wide, 210 mph winds).
🌀
TROPICAL MODE
Hurricane tracking & tropical analysis

Switch to the Tropical tab (🌀) during hurricane season (June 1 – November 30). The sidebar loads tropical-specific layers and a powerful model viewer appears for analyzing track guidance. Recent major storms tracked here include Hurricane Milton (Cat 5, Oct 2024 — rapidly intensified to 180 mph before striking Florida's Gulf Coast near Siesta Key) and Hurricane Helene (Cat 4, Sep 2024 — made landfall near Perry, FL and caused catastrophic inland flooding through the Southern Appalachians).

🌀
NHC FORECAST CONE

The official 5-day track forecast from the National Hurricane Center. The cone shows the probable path of the storm's center. Approximately 2/3 of historical storms stay within the cone — but impacts extend well outside it.

🔵
INVEST AREAS

Disturbances being monitored for development. Numbered 90L–99L (Atlantic) or 90E–99E (East Pacific). For example, Invest 97L in August 2024 eventually became Hurricane Helene. When an invest reaches watch/warning criteria, NHC issues advisories and may name the system.

🌡️
SEA SURFACE TEMP

Critical fuel for tropical systems. Warm water above 26°C (79°F) to a depth of at least 50 meters is generally required to sustain a hurricane. The SST layer uses NOAA's Coral Reef Watch composite.

📊
TROPICAL MODELS

A Tropical Tidbits-style model viewer inside the map. Available models: GFS, ECMWF (Euro), GEFS-Avg, CMC (Canadian), ICON (German), NAM, HWRF, HAFS-A, and HAFS-B. Pick a region and parameter, then step through hours or hit Play.

🛩️
Combine Tropical + Hurricane Hunters: While in Tropical mode, activate the 🛩️ Hurricane Hunters overlay to see NOAA's recon aircraft flying into the storm in real time. Their data feeds directly into NHC's intensity analysis.

Using the Tropical Model Viewer

1
Switch to the Tropical tab and enable the Models layer in the sidebar. The model panel slides in.
2
Choose your Model (GFS, ECMWF, GEFS-Avg, CMC, ICON, NAM, HWRF, HAFS-A, HAFS-B) and Region (Atlantic Basin, W. Atlantic/US East, E. Pacific, C. Pacific, W. Pacific, S. Hemisphere, Indian Ocean, or Global).
3
Select a Parameter: MSLP + 6h Precip, 500mb Vort + Heights, 200mb Wind (Jet Stream), 850mb Wind, 2m Temperature, Total Precip, or Precipitable Water.
4
Pick a Run (model initialization time) and use the frame slider or ▶ Play to animate the forecast.
🖥️
WEATHER MODELS
GFS, NAM, HRRR, SREF, HREF & more

The Models bubble appears in the sidebar only on the Tropical and Severe tabs — it is not available in Regular or Ice mode. Tapping it opens the relevant model panel. A floating info box on the map shows which run is loaded, the resolution, the variable, and current forecast hour.

ModelGFS · NOAA
Run12Z · May 8, 2026
Resolution0.25° (~28 km)
VariableTotal Precip (mm)
Forecast HourF+024h (valid May 9, 12Z)

For severe weather model guidance, switch to the Severe tab which opens a dedicated panel with:

🔢
SREF

Short-Range Ensemble Forecast — a multi-model ensemble highlighting forecast uncertainty in the 0–84 hour range. Useful for identifying where confidence is high versus where solutions diverge. (The legacy SREF was replaced by NCEP's Rapid Ensemble Forecast System in 2021; some platforms still display it as SREF.)

🔢
HREF

High-Resolution Ensemble Forecast — combines HRRR, NAM, and other hi-res models. Excellent for convective initiation timing and QPF (precipitation amount) within 48 hours.

🔢
NAM

North American Mesoscale model — 3km nest available. Standard go-to for mesoscale features, frontal positions, and short-range QPF. Updated 4x daily.

🔢
HRRR

High-Resolution Rapid Refresh — 3km, updated hourly. The gold standard for convective forecasting within 18 hours. Variables include QPF, CAPE, shear, soundings, and hodographs.

Within the Severe model panel you can switch parameters: QPF (precipitation), CAPE (instability), Shear (wind shear), 500mb heights, Hodo (hodograph / storm motion), SRH (storm-relative helicity), and Sounding. Use the run selector and hour slider to step through the forecast.

🛠️
MAP TOOLS
Drawing, animation, compass & more
✏️
DRAW

Opens a floating toolbar. Pick a color from the palette and draw freehand annotations directly on the map. Supports undo/redo. Export your annotated map as a PNG image.

⬡
POLYGON

Draw a closed polygon to create a spatial filter. Once finished, only alerts and data within the drawn region are highlighted. Useful for focusing on a specific county or metro area during an event.

📏
DISTANCE

Click points on the map to measure distances between them. Each segment shows its length and the running total updates as you add points. Double-click to finish. Great for estimating how far a storm is from a location.

〰️
TRACK MAKER

Plot a custom storm track by clicking waypoints. The path connects them in order and can be exported as a PNG. Useful for sketching expected storm paths or comparing against official NHC cone guidance.

▶️
ANIMATION BAR

The bottom bar scrubs through recent radar or satellite frames. Hit Play to loop, adjust speed with the input, or step frame-by-frame. Great for tracking storm motion and estimating where cells will be in 15–30 minutes.

🧭
COMPASS & ROTATION

Use a three-finger rotate gesture on mobile to rotate the map. A compass appears showing your current bearing, and a ↺ Reset button appears — tap it to snap back to north-up.

🗺️
MAP STYLES

Four base map styles available: 🌑 Dark (default, best for radar contrast), 🛰 Satellite (aerial imagery), 🌤 Light (clean minimal), and 🗺 Topo (terrain with elevation). Switch styles from the right-side bubble menu or via ⚙ Settings → Map Style. The right-side menu also has 📍 Locate (center on your GPS position), ✨ Smooth animation toggle, and ⛶ Fullscreen.

Animating Radar

1
Make sure the Radar or Satellite bubble is active in the sidebar.
2
The animation bar at the bottom of the screen shows loaded frames. Each tick is one time step.
3
Press ▶ Play to loop the animation. Use the slider to jump to a specific frame.
4
Watch storm cells move across the map — note direction and speed to estimate where they'll be in 15–30 minutes.
🏆
PRO TIPS
Getting the most out of every feature
🌀 + 🛩️
RECON + NHC COMBO

During active storms: switch to the Tropical tab (which auto-loads NHC cones and SST), then activate the 🛩️ Hurricane Hunters overlay pill. Watch N42RF "Kermit" fly through the eyewall in real time while the forecast cone updates in the background.

⚡
LIVE LIGHTNING

Real-time lightning strikes from the Blitzortung community network. Each bolt appears on the map within seconds of occurring. Toggle the ⚡ pill at any time — works across all modes.

⚠ + 📊
SPC + HRRR

Cross-reference the SPC Day 1 outlook area with HRRR CAPE and shear fields. If the HRRR shows 2000+ J/kg CAPE and 40+ kts of bulk shear inside a Moderate risk, that's a serious setup.

🌥️
FORECAST DOTS

Click multiple forecast dots along a storm's projected path to quickly compare conditions — temperature, humidity, wind — ahead of the storm versus behind it.

📷
WEBCAMS DURING EVENTS

During a tornado warning, check webcams in the warned area for actual visual confirmation. Many cams update every 30–60 seconds and can show wall clouds, funnel clouds, or surface conditions.

🌊
SST FOR INTENSITY

Before a hurricane makes landfall, overlay SST. Warm eddies (Loop Current, Gulf Stream) often cause rapid intensification. Cold upwelling from a slow-moving storm can weaken it.

📱
Mobile use: The map is fully touch-optimized. Pinch to zoom, single-finger pan, two-finger rotate. Overlay pills and tabs are sized for thumb-friendly tapping. In landscape mode you get more map real estate.
🚨
Safety first: This radar is a situational awareness tool. It does not replace official NWS warnings delivered through NOAA Weather Radio, Wireless Emergency Alerts, or local emergency management. Always follow local shelter instructions during active warnings.
